finding.evidence: order 1002 (name, e-mail, address, card ending) returned without any session
finding.description: Any order is readable by changing the number.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: idor (Any order is readable by changing the number. Evidence: order 1002 (name, e-mail, address, card ending) returned without any session). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Enforce server-side authorization on every order access: require an authenticated session and implement access control checks for each object that users try to access, verifying the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object such as database keys, file names, or record IDs before returning data.

sources.contribution: To mitigate IDOR, implement access control checks for each object that users try to access.

IDOR occurs when an application exposes internal object references such as database keys, file names, or record IDs and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.

verification.claim: To mitigate IDOR, implement access control checks for each object that users try to access.
verification.detail: To mitigate IDOR, implement access control checks for each object that users try to access.

verification.claim: IDOR occurs when an application exposes internal object references such as database keys, file names, or record IDs and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.
verification.detail: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) is an access control vulnerability that occurs when an application exposes internal object references — such as database keys, file names, or record IDs — and fails to verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the referenced object.

fix.summary: Require ownership (customer cookie matching order email) or admin session before returning an order, otherwise 403.
fix.risk: Old bookmarked order links without the customer cookie will now get 403 instead of the order.

finding.evidence: response has no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security header
finding.description: Browsers get no instruction against framing, MIME sniffing or script injection.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: missing-security-headers (Browsers get no instruction against framing, MIME sniffing or script injection. Evidence: response has no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security header). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Fix: configure server to send on every HTTPS response: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, plus Content-Security-Policy where frame-ancestors obsoletes X-Frame-Options for supporting browsers. Tune CSP to app.

sources.contribution: Content Security Policy (CSP) frame-ancestors directive obsoletes X-Frame-Options for supporting browsers

verification.detail: Ensure X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set to prevent MIME type sniffing.
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin NOTE: For more information on configuring this header please see Mozilla Referrer-Policy .

verification.claim: Content Security Policy (CSP) frame-ancestors directive obsoletes X-Frame-Options for supporting browsers
verification.detail: Content Security Policy (CSP) frame-ancestors directive obsoletes X-Frame-Options for supporting browsers ( source ).

fix.summary: Add HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and CSP frame-ancestors headers to HTML responses.
fix.risk: Overly restrictive CSP could block legitimate inline scripts or styles in browsers if the pages rely on them.
